source.title: Early effects of SGLT2 inhibitors in acute heart failure: an individual patient-level meta-analysis
source.source_type: individual patient data meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials

findings: Main Table 3 Day-2 weight-change P=.053 conflicts with Supplementary Table S7 fixed-effect P=.008 for the same group medians.
Supplementary Table S5 prints NT-proBNP >=3340 subgroup HR 0.32 with 95% CI 0.38-1.35, an internally impossible interval.
Table 1 prints an EMPAG-HF placebo urine-output IQR with reversed bounds, 6450-3550 mL.
Methods prose gives an eGFR subgroup cutoff unit inconsistent with Table 2 and Supplementary Table S5.
Supplementary Table S6 placebo-only 24-hour raw medians favor placebo while the row reports P=.005 and no effect estimate; no comparative effect was inferred.

schema_gaps: The current LiteratureAtom schema has no dedicated field for meta-analysis-level heterogeneity statistics, so those values remain in canonical statements or provenance rather than a typed heterogeneity object.
The schema has no dedicated representation for a composite hierarchical win-ratio definition beyond OutcomeDescriptor text.
The schema cannot represent conflicting source values as linked alternatives; source-integrity discrepancies are retained as atom_kind="other" with explicit tags.
extraction_limitations: All atoms remain needs_review because no human source-verification action is represented.
Secondary results quoted in Table 1 from the six component RCTs were not promoted to primary-study atoms.
No value with an internally impossible interval or unresolved source-direction conflict was silently corrected.

The filename summary-evaluation-appraisal-protocol-v4-compact.md identifies the governing file as v4, but its internal heading says Integrated Compact v3; the file was followed as supplied and the version-label conflict is reported.
governing_source_issue: The governing SEA file is named v4 but its internal document title says Integrated Compact v3.
external_verification: Publisher HTML was used only to verify article metadata and readable main-table values against the supplied PDF; the source packet remained the extraction basis.
